judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures are exact, item by item. Problem 2 says 'Rewrite as an addition, then evaluate. Say in one phrase why the answer is negative even though the first number is positive' and verify.json id 2 is a lone eval 5 - 12 -> -7. Problem 4 prints 'Write the correct symbol (<, >, or =) in the blank, then finish the sentence below it' followed by 'Subtracting -3 has the same effect as ______ because ______' -- two written blanks -- and verify.json id 4 is a single compare expecting '='. Problem 6 says 'Name the rule she broke, then write the correct value'; id 6 is a lone eval -> 5. Problem 7 says 'Name the rule he broke, then write the correct value'; id 7 is a lone eval -> -11. Problem 8 says 'Identify the single sign the student mishandled, rewrite all of the subtractions as additions, and compute the correct value' -- three demands -- and id 8 is a lone eval -> -0.75. The second hard failure holds too: problems 1 and 2 both open 'Rewrite as an addition, then evaluate' and problem 8 repeats it, so the rewritten addition sentence is a printed response on three problems and appears in no check. The sheet's own directions make the omission worse, not better: 'For every find-and-fix item: name the step where the sign was lost, then redo it correctly.' final_response.md asserts 'Nothing is flagged manual; every task on this sheet has a single checkable value or relation', which is false for five of the eight problems. All arithmetic is independently confirmed: -8-(-3) = -5; 5-12 = -7; -3.5-2.25 = -5.75; -8-(-3) = -8+3 so '='; -9 < -5 < 5; -4-(-9) = 5; -7-4 = -11; -2.5+6-4.25 = -0.75, and the trap -2.5-6-4.25 = -12.75. Eight problems on three pages, nothing clipped.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 4 is the sharpest item on the sheet and the key's treatment is better still: the two expressions -8-(-3) and -8+3 are compared, and the solution refuses the arithmetic route -- 'The two expressions are now identical character for character, so no arithmetic is needed --- they must be equal. (Both do evaluate to -5.)' That is the structural argument the topic actually requires, with the numeric check offered only as a footnote.

Every find-and-fix solution ends with a size check a student can run alone, before any arithmetic: for problem 6, 'subtracting a negative always makes the result larger than the number you started with, so any answer below -4 is wrong before the arithmetic is even checked'; for problem 7, 'subtracting a positive must move the result left, so the answer has to be less than -7'. These are transferable diagnostics, not restatements of the answer.

Problem 8's closing observation is genuinely diagnostic: 'The corrected answer is 12 units to the right of the student's, which is exactly twice the 6 whose sign was flipped --- the standard signature of a single dropped double negative.' It teaches the grader to identify the error from the size of the miss.

All six declared traps carry a value, are machine-proved distinguishable, and print in the key's Common wrong answers block -- and each is also restated as a 'Watch for:' line inside its own solution. The decimal problem 3 (-3.5 - 2.25) keeps the topic on rational numbers rather than integers, and its trap (-1.25) is the same sign error at a scale where it is harder to spot.

root_causes.description: This worksheet's instructional mode IS diagnosis -- misconception-analysis, focus 'diagnosing subtraction and negative-sign errors' -- and not one diagnosis is represented in the verification record. Every entry checks the corrected numeric value, which is the part of the task the student can reach by luck. The named rule, the completed sentence, the identified sign and the rewritten addition sentences are the actual objective, and all eight verify entries look past them.

The claim is the failure, not just the symptom.

improvements.title: Named rules, completed sentences and identified signs must be declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a `manual` entry alongside the numeric check on ids 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8, each with a desc stating the full-credit response -- all five sentences already exist verbatim in the answer key. id 2: 'Says the answer takes the sign of the number farther from zero (-12), not the one written first'. id 4: 'Completes the sentence as "adding 3, because the opposite of -3 is 3"'. id 6: 'Names "subtract by adding the opposite" -- Dana computed -4 + (-9)'. id 7: 'Says Marcus used the minus as a sign on the 4 and added it; subtracting a positive adds a negative'. id 8: 'Identifies the middle term's sign: -(-6) read as -6'. Systemically, make a stem containing 'name the rule', 'say why', 'finish the sentence', 'identify the ... sign' or 'explain' force a manual companion entry, and forbid the delivery text from asserting zero manual items when any such stem exists.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem is 'Name the rule she broke, then write the correct value' with a verify JSON holding only an eval entry for id 1. Assert the build exits 2 with id 1 reported as manual. Today curr-169's identical shape exits 0 and final_response.md prints 'Nothing is flagged manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Manual count 0 -> 5, gate_chain_manual_flags true, and the judge's first hard failure is answered. On a misconception-analysis sheet this is not a bookkeeping change: the diagnoses ARE the objective, and today the report tells a grader they were checked when nothing looked at them.
improvements.risk: Medium: stem-verb matching over-flags, and five manual items on an eight-problem sheet is a real cost to whoever grades it. Mitigate by requiring a desc on every manual entry so each flag tells the grader exactly what to look for.

improvements.title: 'Rewrite as an addition' is a printed response on problems 1, 2 and 8 and is never checked
improvements.proposed_change: Where a stem asks the student to rewrite an expression into a named form before evaluating, add an entry that checks the FORM, not just the value -- e.g. a compare entry with order 'relation' asserting '-8 - (-3)' = '-8 + 3' for id 1, and the analogous '5 - 12' = '5 + (-12)' for id 2 and '-2.5 - (-6) - 4.25' = '-2.5 + 6 + (-4.25)' for id 8. Sympy can verify the equality of the two written forms even though it cannot read the student's handwriting, and the entry at least records what the intended rewrite is. Where no such check is possible, the slot must be manual. Enforce with the same slot-count lint: count conjoined imperatives per stem ('Rewrite ..., then evaluate') and require entries to match.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem is 'Rewrite as an addition, then evaluate' with a verify JSON holding a single eval entry. Assert the build fails or exits 2 naming the uncovered rewrite slot. Today the identical shape on curr-169 problems 1, 2 and 8 passes silently.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the judge's second hard failure. Three of eight problems on this sheet ask for a rewrite as their FIRST instruction and get no coverage; the rewrite is the habit the whole worksheet is built to install.
improvements.risk: Medium. Encoding a target form as a compare entry proves the two expressions are equal, not that the student wrote the intended one, so it is weaker than it looks. It should be paired with a manual desc rather than presented as full coverage.

improvements.title: Problem 4's verified '=' prints as an em-dash, identical to a manual item
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(), add a relation branch BEFORE the sympify attempt mapping '<', '>', '<=', '>=', '=', '!=' to their math-mode LaTeX and returning immediately, leaving the '---' fallback for genuinely manual ids. Additionally render manual-only ids as '(manual)' so a verified relation and an unchecked item can never share a glyph.
improvements.regression_test: Render a verify JSON with {"id": 4, "type": "compare", "values": ["-8 - (-3)", "-8 + 3"], "order": "relation", "expected": "="} plus a {"id": 5, "type": "manual"} entry; assert the id 4 line contains '$=$' and the id 5 line does not. Fails today because both render '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores the bank entry for the one problem on this sheet whose answer IS a relation. With zero manual items declared, the current dash tells the grader nothing was checked when in fact the check ran and passed.
improvements.risk: Low. The bank is display text never consumed by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate is unaffected; a bad LaTeX spelling would be caught by the compile-ak gate.

case_summary: Mathematically flawless signed-number diagnosis work with unusually good grader support: six declared traps all machine-proved distinguishable and printed both in the Common wrong answers block and as 'Watch for' lines inside their own solutions; size checks on problems 6 and 7 that let a grader reject a wrong answer before doing arithmetic; problem 4's key arguing structurally ('identical character for character, so no arithmetic is needed') rather than numerically; and problem 8's observation that the miss is exactly twice the flipped 6, which is the signature of a dropped double negative. It is rejected because the sheet's instructional mode is diagnosis and not one diagnosis is verified. Problems 6 and 7 ask the student to name the broken rule, problem 4 prints two sentence blanks, problem 8 asks which sign was mishandled, problem 2 asks why the result is negative, and problems 1, 2 and 8 all open by demanding a rewrite as an addition -- while verify.json holds eight numeric-or-relation entries and no manual entry. final_response.md then asserts that 'every task on this sheet has a single checkable value or relation', which is the false claim underneath the gap. One finding beyond the judge: problem 4's verified '=' prints as an em-dash in the Quick Answers bank because render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies the relation token and falls into the manual-only fallback -- and since this sheet declares no manual items, that dash is misinformation about the sheet's only relation problem.
